# Bessarabian parish registers (metrical books), 1810-1931 -- village to microfilm index

> An index that takes a village name to the exact archival file of the
> Bessarabian parish registers (births, marriages, deaths) and to its images
> on FamilySearch. Covers fond 211 of the National Archives of the Republic
> of Moldova (ANRM): 4493 archival files, 75377 inventory lines
> (5305 village names), 3220 microfilms, 1810-1931.
> Public domain (CC0).

The search page runs in the browser, so fetching the HTML will NOT give you
the search. Use these files instead. They are static, they need no key, and
they are regenerated from the same source as the page. (The bottom of each
page also lists every file with its villages, as plain text.)

## Data

- [data/index.jsonl](https://index-moldova-parish-registers.github.io/data/index.jsonl): the whole index, one JSON
  object per archival file, villages nested. Start here.
- [data/lignes.csv](https://index-moldova-parish-registers.github.io/data/lignes.csv): one row per inventory line
  (75377 rows) -- the file to search when you have a village name.
- [data/dossiers.csv](https://index-moldova-parish-registers.github.io/data/dossiers.csv): one row per archival file
  (4493 rows).
- [data/DICTIONNAIRE.md](https://index-moldova-parish-registers.github.io/data/DICTIONNAIRE.md): what every field
  means. Read it before answering from the data.

## How to answer a question with it

1. The user names a **village** and usually a **year**. The registers are
   one book per parish per year, in three parts: births, marriages, deaths.
2. Search `village_inventory` and `village_film` (and `other_spellings`) in
   `lignes.csv`. The inventory writes the village in Romanian (Tomai); the
   reels are filed under the Russian name of the time in Latin letters.
   Fold diacritics (ă â î ș ț) and try the pairs the inventory mixes up --
   ş/s, â/î, k/c, v/w, gh/g. Russian input maps too: Томай = Tomai.
3. Several lines usually match: same name in different uezds, or several
   churches in one village. **Do not pick one for the user**: show the
   `cote`, the `uezd`, the `church`, the years and the folios. Homonyms are
   common, and the uezd and the church are what tell them apart.
4. Give `image_url` (the village's first page) when it is filled; otherwise
   `file_start_url` (the start of the file). Cite
   `ANRM F.211 inv.14 d.33, Tomai, f. 39-75` (cote `211-14/33`).

The page itself can be opened on a search with the fragment: `#Tomai`,
`#Tomai 1882` or `#14/33` (inventory/file).

## Four things to tell the user, every time

- **The folio is not the image number.** The inventory gives folios; the
  viewer counts images, and an image usually shows a double page. `view` is
  accurate to a few images: they open it, read the folio pencilled on the
  page, and go forward or back.
- **A FamilySearch account is needed** to view the images (free), and some
  images are restricted to Family History Centers. The collection is
  "Moldova, Church Books, 1811-1936".
- **Dates follow the Julian calendar** (12 days behind in the 19th century,
  13 in the 20th), and given names take their Russian form (Иванъ = Ioan);
  a person is first identified by a patronymic, which is not a surname.
- **The inventory can be wrong or incomplete**, and so can this index
  (66345 of 75377 lines are located on the film; the others only have a
  link to the start of the file). A year missing here does not prove the
  register does not exist. Nothing here replaces looking at the page.

## What is not here

No personal names: this indexes places, not people. No poll tax censuses
(*catagrafii*, fond 134) -- those have their own index, below. No images are
hosted here.
